extracted.intended_audience: former USPTO-registered practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and counsel handling reinstatement petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Petitioning for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; involves filing an affidavit and supporting information and obtaining a Director-level determination from the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file an affidavit in support of the Petition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision notes that Mr. Chen filed an Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; compliance with that regulatory filing requirement is a precondition to consideration. (The page does not restate the content requirements of § 11.58.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Petition must be accompanied by supporting information relevant to the petitioner's eligibility for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office reviewed the Petition, the supporting affidavit, and all information in the record material to his eligibility for reinstatement, indicating that comprehensive supporting documentation and any record materials relevant to eligibility should be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary review and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline reviews the petition, affidavit, and record and determines whether reinstatement is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is granted only after careful review and a discretionary finding by the Director (here, the Director determined reinstatement appropriate and granted the petition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/notice of decision to petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the decision is provided to the petitioner (here, via email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document indicates the mechanism of notice—copy to Mr. Chen via email—so petitioners should expect formal notification of the decision and ensure contact information is current.
